name: skill-card
description: One skill in the marketplace, and the clearest example of why composites-of-composites matter: on the site this is ninety lines that rebuild a card, a badge, a stat and a link relationship by hand, with three variants spelled as three whole class strings rather than as one difference. It composes `card`, `badge` and `stat` and adds only what is genuinely its own — the promise line and the footer rail.

base.transition: border-color var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), transform var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

summary.$description: The measure is in `ch` and it is the reason a grid of these reads: at a fixed pixel width the summaries wrap differently at every card and the row loses its baseline.

rail.$description: `margin-block-start:auto` pins it to the bottom, so a row of cards with summaries of different lengths still lines its rails up. Without it the cards are the same height and the content floats at three different depths.

eyebrow.$description: the plan this skill belongs to. Quiet, because it classifies rather than names.

quote.$description: a founder's own words about the skill. Italic and quiet — it is evidence under the claim, not a second claim.

chains.$description: the other skills this one hands work to. A wrapping row, because the count varies per skill and a fixed row drops the tail.

featured.$description: The one skill a page is steering you towards. A grid where every card is featured is a grid where none is.

soon.$description: Not built yet. A dashed edge and a sunken ground say `placeholder` in a way a fainter fill does not — and the card stays a real link to the waiting list rather than becoming a dead tile.

hover.$description: A lift and a warmer edge. `more` brightens with it, which is why that state names no part: the whole card is one link, so hovering anywhere in it is hovering the link.

reducedMotion.$description: The lift goes, the border still warms.

a11y.note: ONE `<a>` around the whole card. The alternative — a div with an onclick and a `View` link inside — gives a keyboard user two targets for one destination and hands a screen reader a link whose accessible name is the entire card contents. `View` is decoration inside that link, not a second link, which is why it is a `<span>`.
